# tf2perf

**This is AI generated by the HugeGpt 4.1**

Performance hooks for Team Fortress 2. It injects a DLL into the game, hooks a handful of
client-side functions that are expensive on weak CPUs, and gives you a small command line
to turn each one on and off while you play.

Not a virus. The source is right here, there's no network code, and it doesn't write
anything except its own log and config. Details below.

## What it hooks

Every function is found by scanning for byte patterns when the DLL loads, and checked
before it gets patched. If a pattern doesn't match (TF2 update, different build), that hook
just gets skipped and logged. Nothing is ever patched blind.

| Hook | What it does |
|---|---|
| CViewRender::RenderView | frame counter, budget resets, caches the view origin |
| TF_3rdPersonMuzzleFlashCallback (+ sentry) | caps muzzle flash sprites per frame |
| CParticleMgr per-effect simulate | per-frame particle simulation budget |
| C_BaseAnimating::UpdateClientSideAnimations | stops updating far away animations |
| CClientShadowMgr depth pass + PreRender | shadow on/off |
| CEngineVGui::Simulate | VGUI panel logic throttle |
| C_BaseEntity::DrawBrushModel, C_LocalTempEntity::DrawStudioModel | distance culling |
| C_BaseAnimating::SetupBones | skips no-output calls past a distance (experimental) |
| cl_particle_retire_cost | turns on the cheat-flagged particle budget |

## Why antivirus flags it

It's a DLL injector, and basically every injector gets flagged by heuristic scanners. Cheat
Engine, overlay tools and mod loaders all have the same problem. This one doesn't:

- connect to anything (no sockets, no http, nothing)
- write anywhere except %TEMP%\tf2perf.log and its own config file
- touch any process except the TF2 one you point it at
- add startup entries, services or anything that survives a reboot

The only Windows stuff it calls: CreateRemoteThread + LoadLibraryA (injection), MinHook
(detours), CreateNamedPipe (the CLI talks to the DLL over this), fopen (the log). All of it
is in tf2perf.c / tf2perf_cli.c / sigcheck.c, and you can build it yourself.

## VAC warning

This hooks the game process. On VAC servers that can get you banned. Use it on your own
server, on a community server where you accept the risk, or don't use it at all. Not
affiliated with Valve.

## Build

Needs Visual Studio 2022 or newer (x64 C++ tools) and MinHook as a static x64 lib.

1. grab MinHook from github.com/TsudaKageyu/minhook and build libMinHook.x64.lib
2. if it's not in C:\mh, set MINHOOK to the folder
3. run build.cmd

You get tf2perf.dll, tf2perf.exe and sigcheck.exe.

Run sigcheck.exe first if you want. It checks every hook pattern against your client.dll
and engine.dll and should print 14/14 passed. If a TF2 update moves things around, the
hooks that stop matching get skipped at runtime instead of patching the wrong code.

## Usage

```
tf2perf inject      find TF2, inject, drop into the CLI
tf2perf             attach to a game that's already injected
tf2perf status      print hooks and settings once and exit
```

Commands in the CLI:

```
retire 1            particle screen area budget, 0 = off, try 0.5-2
muzzleflash 4       max muzzle flash sprites per frame
simbudget 48        max particle effects simulated per frame
animdist 2000       stop updating animations past 2000 units
shadows off         skip the shadow passes
far 3000            skip brush models and temp ents past 3000 units
vguisim 2           VGUI panel logic every 2nd frame
status              hooks, counters, current settings
alloff              turn every setting off at once
help                full command list
```

The log is at %TEMP%\tf2perf.log.
